root.name: Neo-Grünfeld Defense: Classical Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. g3 Bg7 4. Bg2 O-O 5. O-O d5 6. c4

overview: Both sides fianchetto and Black strikes at the centre with ...d5 against 6.c4. Black chooses between ...c6 (the original defence, solid), ...dxc4 (the modern defence, with Na3 regaining the pawn) and ...c5. White keeps a slight space edge and the long diagonal; Black tries for ...c5 or ...e5 and active piece play.

white_ideas.idea: Nc3, cxd5 and a centre pawn pair with the bishop on g2
After ...dxc4 play Na3 and Nxc4 to regain the pawn

black_ideas.idea: ...c6 and ...Bf5 or ...Nbd7 with a compact centre

typical_structures.structure: Grünfeld-like centre where White holds d4/c4 and Black has ...c6 or ...c5 against it

character.notes: Positional, with both fianchettos; less tactical than the real Grünfeld.

gambit.notes: After 6...dxc4 White regains the pawn by force.

structure.notes: Centre is tense with ...d5 against c4 and d4; not locked.

approach.notes: A standard hypermodern branch for Black against 1.d4.

level.notes: Needs a feel for the pawn breaks; theory is moderate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Modern Defense 6...dxc4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. g3 Bg7 4. Bg2 O-O 5. O-O d5 6. c4 dxc4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes the pawn and White regains it with tempo; sharper piece play.

character.reason: Neither a rock-solid nor a forcing main line.

gambit.reason: Pawn on c4 comes back by force.

approach.reason: Played by strong players against one set-up, not a universal system.

level.reason: Plans take judgement; theory is limited.

plans.reason: Both sides use the long diagonals and fight for the centre.
